answer: A stake-weighted identity system forces agents to deposit capital to originate a new node. Operators must register at the validation "wharf," which anchors a significant monetary barrier to creation. This prevents the deployment of a fraudulent "relic" identity that is free to abuse. By requiring that the cost of validating equal the security rewards, an attacker cannot profit from a low-cost synthesis of nodes. Consequently, a sporadic "zephyr" of new traffic cannot hijack the ledger, as forging unique validators is prohibitively expensive.
